item.title: Villa fail to close gap on top spot
item.description: Aston Villa suffered a 1-nil defeat at home to 10-man Brentford - missing the chance to cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the Premier League. Second-placed Manchester City can close that gap to 4 points if they beat Tottenham Hotspur this afternoon. Manchester United scored in stoppage time to make it three straight wins under Michael Carrick with a dramatic 3-2 victory at home to Fulham. Advertisement Nottingham Forest drew 1-all with Crystal Palace to edge 6 points clear of the bottom three.

item.title: Kerry councillor calls for social media companies to face more legal liability
item.description: Social media companies should be held to the same legal standards as broadcasters and newspapers, according to a Kerry County Councillor. Fianna Fáil councillor Breandán Fitzgerald made the call at the recent full meeting of Kerry County Council. He's urging Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan and Innovation and Science Minister James Lawless to bring in legislation treating social media companies as publishers under Irish law. item.title: Waiting times for driving tests at Kerry centres within 10-week service level agreement
item.description: Driving test waiting times in both Kerry testing centres are operating within the 10-week service level agreement. That's according to the most recent report from the RSA to Minister of State Sean Canney, which was released today. Wait times in Killarney are currently 8 weeks, while learner drivers will have to wait ten weeks to sit their test in the Tralee centre. item.title: Man City extend WSL lead
item.description: Manchester City have thrashed Chelsea 5-1 and lead the Women's Super League by 11 points with 8 games to play. The defending champions are now 12 points off the top, their title defence in tatters. Manchester United have gone second after beating bottom team Liverpool 3-1. Advertisement Tottenham, in fifth, join Arsenal on 26 points after winning 2-1 at strugglers West Ham. item.title: Celtic win
item.description: Celtic are up to second in the Scottish Premiership thanks to a 2-nil win at home to Falkirk. They've moved six points behind leaders Hearts. Old Firm rivals Rangers drop to third on goal difference after being held nil-nil at Hibs. Advertisement
